purpose: Teach: 恵比寿/坊主/生きがい/本命/クラフト/柵/ムーン/フランクフルト

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、恵比寿のあたり、本当に、よく、デート、したよな、ばあさん、覚えてる、楽しい思い出、たくさん、ある。
lines.en: When I was young, we used to go on dates around Ebisu all the time. You remember, don't you? We have so many happy memories from those days.
lines.style: Soft opening, voice settling into the past. Warm but distant — reaching back. Gentle rhythm, unhurried. Slight lift at the end, turning toward her.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。隣の坊主さん、近所のお世話を、本当に、よく、してくれていたわね、覚えてる、あなた、感謝しないとね、本当に。
lines.en: Yes. And that monk next door — he did so much to help with the neighborhood, didn't he? I remember. We really should have thanked him more.
lines.style: Agreeing gently, then thoughtful. Voice brightens slightly on the memory of the monk, then softens into quiet gratitude. Reflective, almost speaking to herself.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 退職後、孫の世話が、私の生きがいになったな、ばあさん、本当に、毎日、楽しいんだ、孫って、本当に、宝物だ。
lines.en: After I retired, taking care of our grandchildren became what I lived for. Every day is truly enjoyable. Grandchildren — they're real treasures.
lines.style: Voice lifts with genuine warmth. Speaking with quiet conviction, not bragging. Slight pause before 'treasures' — the word carries full weight. Steady, present.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃のあなたの本命、私だったのよね?他にも、いたんでしょ、本当に、教えて、もう、時効よ、覚えてる?
lines.en: But wait — back when you were young, I was your only one, wasn't I? Or were there others? Come on, tell me — the statute of limitations is up by now. Do you remember?
lines.style: Playful, slightly teasing. A little sharper than before but still affectionate. Quick rhythm, dancing a bit. Expecting to catch him in something. Light and alive.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔、私、木工、クラフト、よく、やったな、ばあさん、覚えてる?家族に、いろいろ、作ってあげたよな、本当に、楽しかった。
lines.en: I used to do a lot of woodworking and crafts back then. You remember, don't you? I made so many things for the family. It was really enjoyable.
lines.style: Gentle, nostalgic opening. Voice softens around the memory. Slower pace, almost wondering aloud. Trailing off slightly — lost in the simple pleasure of having made things.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 庭の柵、お祖父ちゃんが、若い頃に、自分で、作ってくれたものよね、覚えてる、あなた、何度も、塗り直したよね、本当に。
lines.en: That fence in the garden — your grandfather built it himself when he was young. Do you remember? We repainted it so many times over the years.
lines.style: Warm and precise, like she can see it clearly. Speaking with affection and gentle pride in his work. The 'so many times' carries lived experience, not complaint. Steady voice.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔、アポロのムーンランディング、テレビで、二人で、見たわよね、ばあさん、感動したよな、覚えてる、本当に。
lines.en: When we watched the Apollo moon landing on television together, I was so moved. You remember that, don't you? It was truly something.
lines.style: Voice reaches back with wonder. Slow, almost reverent rhythm. Genuine emotion — not performed, but fully present. A pause before 'truly' — the weight of having witnessed it together.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 戦後、初めて、フランクフルトソーセージ、食べたとき、本当に、衝撃だったわよね、あなた、覚えてる、私、忘れない。
lines.en: Right after the war, when I ate a frankfurter for the first time, it was such a shock. You remember, don't you? I never forgot that taste.
lines.style: Bright, almost laughing at the memory. Warm surprise in her voice — the small miracle of tasting something new. Intimate, like she's looking right at him. Not sad, just vividly alive in the moment.
